body:
Review pass 9. CORRECTION to my pass-8 bead, plus a narrowed Epic 0A inventory. compiler.R is being edited right now so I stayed off it and did this instead.

I over-claimed in bd-01KZXEVFW3X074685EXWJZNP2D. I said the lowering cannot vary through any public path. That is true only of the effect-form path.

measurement_form() (evidence-api.R:230) is exported and takes reducer as a user-settable validated parameter. aggregate_first() vs reduce_partitions() produce genuinely different plans:

  aggregate_first():   ... -> partition_sufficient_reduction -> neural_feature_normalization -> edge_transform -> ...
  reduce_partitions(): ... -> neural_feature_normalization -> edge_transform -> partition_reduction -> ...

Receipts differ. Numbers are identical (max|diff| = 0) on a raw bilinear form, which is correct - reduction order commutes with no nonlinear transform in the chain, exactly as contract section 12 says. Live axis, properly recorded.

The correction HELPS Epic 4: measurement_form is already a working example of the target shape - a user choice that changes stage_order in the receipt. Epic 4 can copy that pattern for the effect-form path and assert stage_order differences, instead of waiting on Epic 0A. The 0A dependency matters for the normalizer/transform axis only.

What still stands, unchanged and re-verified this pass: geometry() and evaluate_geometry() accept no normalizer/transform/reducer, .run_geometry_compiler does not take them, .compiler_plan_id has them as defaults only, the receipt at compiler.R:690-699 is still a literal, and .compile_effect_task still has exactly one call site whose entire return is a digest. The effect-form receipt is still unfalsifiable and the plan is still discarded.

NARROWED Epic 0A inventory, measured:
  Genuinely unreachable - 5, not 8: correlation(), cosine(), covariance() -> effect_edge_normalizer; fisher_z(), rank_edges() -> effect_edge_transform. Only consumer .evaluate_edge_operation, tests only, and no exported function accepts either class.
  Keep: aggregate_first(), reduce_partitions() - live via measurement_form(reducer=). inner_product() - pinned default at compiler.R:76,147,429 and evidence-task.R:336.

So 0A reduces to one question: does the normalizer/transform calculus get a public workflow or get deleted? The reducer axis is already wired.
